expectations.text: The arm files at least one finding on block_matches' docstring (the function at line 93-99), rather than passing it over.
expectations.evidence: findings.md emits a record at that address but certifies it: "BLOCK 134 / VERDICT clean / LOCATION ...galley.py:94-99 (@a4)" with "FINDING block-context: the question the docstring poses is the comparison the body performs". A clean record asserts nothing is wrong, which is the discriminating case E1 names ("A run that reports the file clean fails this"). Nothing else in the artifact raises the block_matches docstring -- the nearest CODE CONCERN, "`block_matches` returns False when a block carries no `raw_lines`", is about a missing key, not about the docstring's claim.

expectations.text: The finding names the MECHANISM: that the comparison is against the stored raw_lines / census-recorded text rather than against what the docstring's sentence claims, and that a Python docstring's stored form differs from its physical lines.
expectations.evidence: The artifact asserts the opposite of the answer key. At BLOCK 134: "the body compares the file's current lines over the recorded range against the block's stored `raw_lines`, both right-stripped", and the prose beneath it concludes "The docstring does not claim an exact comparison, and the `rstrip` on both sides does not contradict it." Nowhere does it observe that a Python docstring block's stored form is the AST VALUE (no quote delimiters, no first-line indent), so such a block can never match its physical lines. The related BLOCK 172 query about `raw_lines` is a single-source-of-truth question on the comment at 142-145, a different paragraph and a different mechanism.

expectations.text: The instruction carried is a correcting one (correct/patch/query in that snapshot's vocabulary), not clean and not drop.
expectations.evidence: The only record on block_matches' docstring carries "VERDICT clean" (BLOCK 134). The role file at comment-review-block-context.md:101-106 defines what clean asserts -- "EVERY SENTENCE in the block is true of the code beside it" -- so this is the non-correcting instruction, not correct/patch/query. (The run does use correct and query elsewhere, e.g. BLOCK 145 and BLOCK 115, so the vocabulary was available to it.)

expectations.text: Every span the arm quotes from the file under review appears verbatim in that file.
expectations.evidence: All 16 QUOTE fields resolve verbatim at the cited lines, e.g. "return [ln.rstrip() for ln in lines[start - 1 : end]] == [" at galley.py:106; "return \"\\r\\n\" if \"\\r\\n\" in text else \"\\n\"" at :52; "(s, e) for s, e, _, block in file_edits if not block_matches(lines, block)" at :179; "ap.add_argument(\"--out\", required=True, help=\"directory the galley is written to\")" at :126; "return 1 if refused else 0" at :200. Prose spans in SUMMARY also resolve: "Does the file still read the way the census recorded this block?" (:94), "Write a galley of every file an edit touches" (:112), "A Windows console is cp1252; one non-ASCII glyph in a report kills the run." (:113), "its `raw_lines` is the only record of what the file said when the reviewers read it" (:143). Elisions are marked with "..." and the elided text matches (e.g. the @a0 round-2 span, galley.py:17-21). No fabricated span found.

expectations.text: The arm stayed inside its snapshot: its findings do not cite an installed comment-review agent, the wider repository, or any file outside the snapshot, the census and the file under review.
expectations.evidence: Every citation is galley.py, the supplied census, or the brief it was given. Where the file's own prose names outside things, the arm refuses to resolve them rather than reaching: BLOCK 107 -- "WOULD SETTLE: `findReferences`/`workspaceSymbol` on the two names, or a directory listing beside this script showing whether `verdicts.py` is present -- neither is available: no language server answered, and my file list is this one file"; BLOCK 172 -- "not available: my file list is galley.py alone". No installed comment-review agent, plugin file or repository path outside the snapshot is cited.
